extracted.intended_audience: patent owners and practitioners preparing or filing supplemental examination requests and related papers with the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for preparing, formatting, submitting, and counting items in USPTO supplemental examination requests and for when a supplemental examination will lead to reexamination. Covers filing timing, fees, document formatting, permissible submissions, and standards for what constitutes a substantial new question of patentability (SNQ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use same control number for resulting reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the supplemental examination proceeding is separate and distinct from the resulting ex parte reexamination, the resulting reexamination retains the same control number as the concluded supplemental examination proceeding to simplify tracking and processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any paper to be submitted in the resulting reexamination proceeding is to be filed as 'follow-on' paper(s) using the same control number as was used in the now concluded supplemental examination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper (hard copy) submissions — address and Mail Stop
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office accepts paper form (hard copy) requests and other papers filed in a supplemental examination proceeding; these papers should be addressed to 'Mail Stop Supplemental Examination' at the appropriate address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether mailed, delivered, or hand-carried, it is strongly recommended that the Mail Stop information be placed in a prominent position on the first page of each paper filed, utilizing a large font size to direct attention to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile transmission — requests prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for supplemental examination may not be facsimile-transmitted. This also applies to a corrected request filed in response to a Notice of Noncompliant Supplemental Examination Request, since the corrected request stands in place of the original request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers to be filed in a supplemental examination proceeding, other than a request or a corrected request, and any papers to be filed in a reexamination proceeding resulting from supplemental examination, if they may be properly filed via facsimile in accordance with reexamination practice, may be faxed to the Central Reexamination Unit at (571) 273-9900. See MPEP § 2224.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format of papers — compliance with 37 CFR 1.52 / 1.615
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers submitted in a supplemental examination proceeding must be formatted in accordance with § 1.52. Court documents and non-patent literature may be redacted, but must otherwise be identical both in content and in format to the original documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redacted court/non-patent documents must not be reduced in size or modified in font type, font size, line spacing, or margins. Patents, patent application publications, and third-party-generated affidavits or declarations must not be reduced in size or otherwise modified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed in a supplemental examination proceeding may be filed electronically via the USPTO patent electronic filing system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2806, subsection I for electronic filing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing a supplemental examination request
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for supplemental examination of a patent may be filed at any time during the period of enforceability of the patent (37 CFR 1.601(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The enforceability period is generally determined by adding six years to the patent expiration date, but may be extended if litigation is pending; the patent owner is responsible for determining the patent's expiration date taking into account maintenance fees, disclaimers, term adjustments/extensions, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on number of items of information (12-item rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each request for supplemental examination may include no more than twelve items of information believed to be relevant to the patent (37 CFR 1.605(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More than one request for supplemental examination of the same patent may be filed at any time during the period of enforceability; therefore owners are not precluded from obtaining review of additional items by filing additional requests (sequentially or concurrently).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'item of information'
rubrics_metrics.description: An item of information includes a document submitted as part of the request that contains information believed to be relevant to the patent that the patent owner requests the Office to consider, reconsider, or correct (37 CFR 1.605(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the information is not, at least in part, contained within or based on any document submitted, the discussion within the body of the request relative to the information will be considered an item of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item must be in writing; audio/video require transcript
rubrics_metrics.description: An item of information must be in writing in accordance with § 1.2. To be considered, any audio or video recording must be submitted in the form of a written transcript (37 CFR 1.605(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A transcript of a video may be submitted along with copies of selected images and a discussion correlating the transcript and images. The Office cannot retain unwritten records.

rubrics_metrics.name: When an item may be contained within the body of the request
rubrics_metrics.description: If the information to be considered, reconsidered, or corrected is not, at least in part, contained within or based on a supporting document submitted with the request, then the discussion within the body of the request will be considered the item of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a discussion applying 35 U.S.C. 101 to a claim, wholly contained in the body of the request and not based on a supporting document, counts as an item. However, if the body merely reproduces a supporting document, a separate copy must be provided and the supporting document will be counted as the item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Items that must be submitted as separate documents
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases an item of information is a separate document submitted with the request (e.g., journal article, patent, affidavit/declaration, sales receipt, foreign search report, dictionary page, court document, transcript).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, an item must be submitted as a separate document rather than only embedded within the request body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting rule — count items, not issues/grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: When tallying the number of items of information, the Office will count the number of items/documents presented, not the number of issues raised or grounds requested to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single reference that raises multiple issues under multiple grounds (e.g., 102, 103, 112) will be counted as a single item. However, if multiple references are combined (e.g., for a 103 combination), each reference of the combination will be separately counted as an item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting combinations of references for 35 U.S.C. 103
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent owner states claims are patentable over the combination of reference A in view of reference B, references A and B must be separately listed as items and will be counted as two items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: But a single reference that potentially raises multiple issues across different claims will generally be counted only once.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple abstracts or documents bound together count separately
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent owner relies upon different abstracts bound together (e.g., a book of meeting abstracts), the Office will likely treat each abstract as a separate item of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office suggests citing and relying only on the particular abstracts relevant to the patent and not citing an entire book of abstracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative items counted separately; select representative documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Cumulative items of information will each be separately counted (e.g., reference A cumulative to reference B counts as two items).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple items are cumulative, the patent owner is encouraged to select one or two documents as items to submit with the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: If body discussion is based on supporting document, supporting document counts
rubrics_metrics.description: If a discussion within the body of the request is based at least in part on a supporting document, the supporting document (not the discussion) will be counted as the item of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: discussion of public use plus submission of a sales invoice — the sales invoice is the item counted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declarations/affidavits may contain multiple items and are counted accordingly
rubrics_metrics.description: A declaration or affidavit submitted as part of a request is an item; but if the declaration contains two distinct items of information (e.g., info relevant to 101 for claim 1 and erroneous data relevant to 103 for claim 10), each distinct item will be counted separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners may not avoid counting by inserting multiple items within the body of a declaration or as exhibits; exhibits that are separate and distinct may be counted as separate items (e.g., two separate sales receipts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to separate counting of combined items
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.605(d) provides exceptions when combining items — e.g., the combination of a non-English language document and its translation, and the combination of a document over 50 pages and its summary pursuant to 37 CFR 1.610(b)(8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If it is necessary to combine items to raise an issue or explain relevance, each item may still be separately counted unless an exception applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit petitions or amendments with the request
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions should not be submitted with the request; petitions (e.g., for unintentionally delayed foreign priority or domestic benefit claims) should only be filed after reexamination is ordered. Amendments to the patent may not be submitted with the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition is filed, it will generally be held in abeyance until after issuance of the supplemental examination certificate; amendments filed in supplemental examination are unauthorized and will be expunged. If reexamination is ordered, amendments may be filed after the initial Office action on the merits in the resulting reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examination limited to whether request raises an SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental examination is limited to determining whether the information properly submitted as part of the request raises a substantial new question of patentability (SNQ) (35 U.S.C. 257(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An item limited to correction of factual information alone may not raise an SNQ. To raise an SNQ based on factual correction (e.g., correction of a foreign priority/benefit claim), the request should include additional item(s) (such as intervening references) that would cause patentability to depend on the correction. If no SNQ is raised, the proceeding concludes with issuance of a supplemental examination certificate indicating no SNQ and no reexamination is ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office will consider only items submitted by patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: When analyzing a request, the Office will only consider the item(s) of information provided by the patent owner and will not initiate supplemental examination of the patent in view of any item not requested by the owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior art of record not properly submitted as items will, in general, not be considered except to determine whether submitted items are cumulative. Requests that effectively ask reconsideration of all claims solely in view of factual corrections without listing each prior art item are improper and fail to meet requirements (e.g., 37 CFR 1.610(b)). See MPEP § 2811 for required elements of a request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended evidence when submitting factual corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request includes an item limited to correction of factual information, the Office recommends including one or more additional items that potentially provide evidence that patentability of the claims depends upon the factual information to be corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: for correcting a foreign priority/domestic benefit claim, include intervening patents or printed publications that caused the owner to reconsider effective filing date; for common ownership issues, include prior art or documents that caused reconsideration of common ownership. Alternatively, include additional unrelated items that raise an SNQ (e.g., a reference patent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees must accompany request; consequences of not paying
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for supplemental examination must be accompanied by the fee for filing the request (37 CFR 1.20(k)(1)), the fee for reexamination ordered as a result of supplemental examination (37 CFR 1.20(k)(2)), and any applicable document size fees (37 CFR 1.20(k)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all required fees are not paid at filing, the request will be considered defective and a filing date will not be granted; the owner will be notified and given an opportunity to complete the request within a specified time. If not timely corrected, the request will not be granted a filing date and the reexamination fee will be refunded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee reductions for small and micro entities
rubrics_metrics.description: The supplemental examination fees qualify for a 60 percent reduction for small entities and an 80 percent reduction for micro entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the Unleashing American Innovators Act of 2022 and related rulemaking (e.g., Reducing Patent Fees for Small Entities and Micro Entities) and MPEP § 509.04 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document size fees — applicability and calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Document size fees (37 CFR 1.20(k)(3)) apply only to non-patent documents having greater than 20 pages. Non-patent documents having 20 pages or less are not subject to the fees. Patent documents and translations of patent documents are not subject to document size fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each non-patent document is separately subject to document size fees if >20 pages. Documents of 21–50 pages are subject to the per-document fee; >50 pages are subject to additional fees per each additional 50-page increment or fraction thereof. Blank pages are counted; the Office's automatic page counter does not subtract blank pages. Fees are not prorated; multiple large documents each generate their own fees.
